return.specificity: Reads as authored for AAC: ready-for-human queue, lander run on AAC-AI, Central-time landing windows, Recommended option with a Then: consequence. No generic tells. Sample data is synthetic, so the footer reads Storage unavailable.

heuristic_notes.1: Footer progress and Landed lines show status. Queue position after Submit is not visible. The offline notice is a plain gray sentence.
heuristic_notes.2: Plain labels with consequences. The chips blocked by and holding up do not say what they mean for the pick.
heuristic_notes.3: Skip, change your mind and Other are stated. No clear or undo control is visible for a pick.
heuristic_notes.4: Consistent cards, chips and one accent. The Recommended pill and the chips share an outline shape.
heuristic_notes.5: Submit is disabled with words. The bulk pick button has a caveat but no count or confirmation.
heuristic_notes.6: Everything needed is on the card. #101 and #102 refer to each other across cards.
heuristic_notes.7: Bulk pick, tabs, phone select and sticky footer. No jump to the next unanswered card.
heuristic_notes.8: Clean, stat tiles gone. The two-column pair leaves empty space on desktop and stacks long on phones.
heuristic_notes.9: Change-your-mind is stated. No error, failed-landing or undo state is visible in any screenshot.
heuristic_notes.10: Intro, GitHub queue link and lander timing give destination. The timing sentence is dense.

personas.name: Jordan
red_flags: Intro paragraph, three bullets and a timing sentence come before the first card.
The chips blocked by #101 and needs you are not explained, and #102 gives no hint to answer #101 first.
The bulk button does not name its count or scope.

personas.name: Sam
red_flags: At 200% zoom the layout reflows to one column and stays readable.
The Then: consequence line is the lightest text in the card.
In forced colors the question band loses its tint, but meaning stays in words.

personas.name: Riley
red_flags: The Note box has room for a long Other note.
At 390 px the page is 3196 px tall for two cards and the footer wraps Submit under the progress line.
The offline Submit looks the same as the online disabled one, so a failed save is easy to miss.

strengths: One accent hue, native radios, and state carried by words and weight. Holds in forced-colors and reduced-motion.
Each option states its consequence and Recommended is marked clearly.
No horizontal scroll at 390, tabs become a select, 200% zoom reflows.

issues.what: The storage-unavailable state is one small gray caption under the progress line, and Submit looks like its normal disabled state.
issues.why: A person can pick on several cards believing it saves. The failure is silent apart from caption text.
issues.fix: Add a bordered top-of-page banner with bold words and keep the footer line.

issues.what: Intro, three facts and timing sentence sit before the first card.
issues.why: A repeat visitor scrolls past them every time, and at 390 px they fill much of the first screen.
issues.fix: Collapse the facts into a How this works disclosure and shorten the timing sentence.

issues.what: Pick every recommended option here has no count and no undo.
issues.why: One click can set many rulings and finding which moved is slow.
issues.fix: Show the count on the button and an undo line after the click.

issues.what: On phones the explainer, issue text and wrapped footer push the first question far down.
issues.why: Scrolling loses context and multiplies over 40 cards.
issues.fix: Collapse explainer detail on phones, put Submit on the progress row, show the question first.

issues.what: Relationship chips are unlinked outlines and look like the Recommended pill.
issues.why: The owner cannot jump to the related card.
issues.fix: Make chips anchor links and give Recommended a different shape.

minor: The Then: line is the lightest text and carries the consequence.
The stitched footer and tab bar in full-page captures are a capture artifact and not scored.
